name: @neat.is/mcp

tools.name: ask
tools.description: Ask the graph a question in plain language — the front door to NEAT. Reach for this FIRST, before Read/Grep/Bash, for any question about this system's behaviour, dependencies, failures, root cause, or blast radius. You do NOT need to know which tool or the exact node id: `ask` resolves the entities in your question to graph nodes and routes it to the right traversal (root cause, dependencies, observed runtime calls, incidents, divergences, blast radius), returning one compact answer with every fact provenance-tagged (EXTRACTED/OBSERVED/INFERRED/STALE) and confidence-scored. Ask what a node talks to, connects to, uses, hits, calls, reads from, or writes to for dependencies; add actually, in production, or at runtime for observed calls. Ask who calls or depends on a node, or for its consumers or callers, for blast radius. Ask about slow, latency, p95, or timing for runtime evidence; a why/failure question leads with root cause. Use the structured tools (get_root_cause, get_dependencies, …) when you already have a node id and want just that one traversal. When something is failing, investigate returns the whole incident in one call.

question.description: A natural-language question, e.g. "why is checkout failing?" or "what breaks if I change the orders table?"

project.description: Project name when the core hosts more than one (set NEAT_PROJECTS=...). Omit to use the default project.

tools.name: get_root_cause
tools.description: Why is a node failing? Trace the failing node up its dependency graph toward likely root-cause candidates, ranked with per-candidate classification (primary-failure vs downstream symptom). Returns a provenance-scored cause chain and recorded error context that file search cannot establish from runtime evidence. For the whole work order on a failure, call investigate or get_incident_card first.

errorNode.description: Graph node id where the error surfaced, e.g. "database:payments-db"

errorId.description: Specific error event id from incident history; if set, the result is coloured with that error message

project.description: Project name when the core hosts more than one (set NEAT_PROJECTS=...). Omit to use the default project.

tools.name: get_blast_radius
tools.description: What depends on this node — what breaks if I change it? Before changing or redeploying a node, see its downstream dependents and evidence-bearing paths. Returns the bounded blast radius so an edit plan includes the affected services, routes, data, and callers.

nodeId.description: Graph node id to compute blast radius from

project.description: Project name when the core hosts more than one (set NEAT_PROJECTS=...). Omit to use the default project.

tools.name: get_dependencies
tools.description: What does this node depend on? Map a node's outgoing dependencies across code, data, and infrastructure. Returns a bounded traversal (default depth 3, max 10) with distance, edge type, provenance, and confidence; depth=1 shows direct dependencies only.

depth.description: BFS depth (default 3, max 10). depth=1 returns direct dependencies only.

project.description: Project name when the core hosts more than one (set NEAT_PROJECTS=...). Omit to use the default project.

tools.name: get_observed_dependencies
tools.description: What did this node actually call at runtime? Return only its OBSERVED outgoing dependencies, from spans or supported provider signals. Compare with get_dependencies or get_divergences to tell declared intent from seen behavior.

project.description: Project name when the core hosts more than one (set NEAT_PROJECTS=...). Omit to use the default project.

tools.name: expand
tools.description: Walk one evidence-bearing hop from a node after investigate or an incident card points to a locus. "up" finds callers/dependents and "down" finds callees/dependencies; each neighbor is classified primary-failure, symptom-only, or unrelated so you can separate cause from downstream symptoms.

nodeId.description: Graph node id to step from

direction.description: up = callers/dependents (toward the cause), down = callees/dependencies

project.description: Project name when the core hosts more than one (set NEAT_PROJECTS=...). Omit to use the default project.

tools.name: relate
tools.description: Are these two nodes cause and symptom? Test a suspected cause-and-symptom pair. Returns a bounded connecting path, direction, per-hop provenance, and whether error/latency signal carries end to end. No path within the bound is reported as such, not as proof the nodes are unrelated.

project.description: Project name when the core hosts more than one (set NEAT_PROJECTS=...). Omit to use the default project.

tools.name: get_incident_history
tools.description: What failed here, and when? Read a node's recorded error events — incidents, crashes, exceptions — most recent first, with their deploy/env context. The incident ledger preserves failure evidence and timestamps a source search cannot reveal.

project.description: Project name when the core hosts more than one (set NEAT_PROJECTS=...). Omit to use the default project.

tools.name: get_incident_card
tools.description: Compose the incident work order for an exact node id (a service, file, or symbol): the recorded incident, likely cause chain, blast radius, governing policies, and divergences, each claim provenance-tagged — the same card NEAT pushes when it detects a failure. Have a symptom or a bare service name instead of a node id? Call investigate; it resolves the name and composes this card. Omit errorId for the latest incident or pin a specific one, then use expand/relate to verify the path.

nodeId.description: Graph node id the incident is on (service/file/symbol)

errorId.description: Pin a specific incident by its id; omit for the most recent

project.description: Project name when the core hosts more than one (set NEAT_PROJECTS=...). Omit to use the default project.

tools.name: investigate
tools.description: First call for a failing, slow, or crashing system. Give it a service name, a symptom ("why are reservations failing"), or a node id, and it returns the composed incident for the node it resolves: the recorded failure with its deploy/env context, the likely root cause and its provenance, the blast radius, the governing policies, and where declared and observed behavior diverge — one work order instead of several queries. Resolves a bare name to its service node, or the best graph match for a symptom; then use expand/relate to verify the chain. Same card get_incident_card composes from an exact node id, and the card NEAT pushes when it detects a failure.

target.description: A service name ("payments"), a symptom ("why is checkout failing"), or a node id ("service:payments")

errorId.description: Pin a specific incident by its id; omit for the most recent

project.description: Project name when the core hosts more than one (set NEAT_PROJECTS=...). Omit to use the default project.

tools.name: semantic_search
tools.description: When you cannot name a graph node, find candidate nodes by a natural-language description. Searches node labels through Ollama nomic-embed-text when reachable, then in-process MiniLM, then substring fallback; it does not search arbitrary source contents. MiniLM downloads a ~23 MB quantized model on a cold cache; set NEAT_SEARCH_PROVIDER=substring before daemon startup to avoid model initialization and download.

query.description: Free-text query, e.g. "service handling checkout payments"

project.description: Project name when the core hosts more than one (set NEAT_PROJECTS=...). Omit to use the default project.

tools.name: get_graph_diff
tools.description: What changed since a known-good point? Compare a saved snapshot with the live graph. Returns added, removed, and changed nodes and edges plus both timestamps, so architecture drift and regressions are visible beyond a file diff.

againstSnapshot.description: Path or http(s) URL of the snapshot to diff against (the "before" state). The current graph is the "after".

project.description: Project name when the core hosts more than one (set NEAT_PROJECTS=...). Omit to use the default project.

tools.name: get_recent_stale_edges
tools.description: What traffic or integration went quiet? List recent OBSERVED → STALE edge transitions — the edges that stopped being seen, and when. Quiet is a signal to investigate, not proof the dependency is healthy or removed.

edgeType.description: Filter by edge type — e.g. "CALLS" or "CONNECTS_TO"

project.description: Project name when the core hosts more than one (set NEAT_PROJECTS=...). Omit to use the default project.

tools.name: get_divergences
tools.description: Where do the code and what's actually running disagree? Return ranked divergences between declared code/config and observed behavior: missing edges, version or host mismatches, compatibility violations, symbol/field mismatches, and observed failures. Each carries confidence and severity; use it for a broad audit before choosing a specific failing node.

type.description: Filter by divergence type. One or more of: missing-observed, missing-extracted, version-mismatch, host-mismatch, compat-violation, observed-symbol-mismatch, observed-failing. Omit for all.

minConfidence.description: Drop divergences below this confidence threshold (0.0 - 1.0).

node.description: Scope to divergences involving this node id (as source or target).

project.description: Project name when the core hosts more than one (set NEAT_PROJECTS=...). Omit to use the default project.

tools.name: check_policies
tools.description: Before an edit, ask which architectural policies apply to its node; before a proposed action, dry-run its policy effect. Returns advisory rules or violations across structure, compatibility, provenance, ownership, and blast radius. Policies inform the agent; this tool does not block changes.

hypotheticalAction.description: Dry-run mode: simulate the action and return resulting violations. Omit for current state.

applicableTo.description: Soft guardrail (ADR-108): pass the node id you are about to edit and check_policies returns the policies that govern it, as a context block — so you stay inside the lines. Advisory only; never blocks.

project.description: Project name when the core hosts more than one (set NEAT_PROJECTS=...). Omit to use the default project.

tools.name: neat_list_uninstrumented
tools.description: When the graph lacks expected runtime evidence, list project libraries outside automatic instrumentation coverage. Returns first-party, third-party, and gap libraries that may need an explicit instrumentation package.

project.description: Project name when the core hosts more than one (set NEAT_PROJECTS=...). Omit to use the default project.

tools.name: neat_lookup_instrumentation
tools.description: When a library is an instrumentation gap, look up its supported registry recipe. Returns the instrumentation package, matching version range, and registration snippet when one exists.

project.description: Project name when the core hosts more than one (set NEAT_PROJECTS=...). Omit to use the default project.

tools.name: neat_describe_project_instrumentation
tools.description: When OBSERVED evidence is missing, inspect this project's instrumentation wiring. Returns hook-file presence, .env.neat presence, and installed OTel dependencies before you change code.

project.description: Project name when the core hosts more than one (set NEAT_PROJECTS=...). Omit to use the default project.

tools.name: neat_apply_extension
tools.description: After reviewing an instrumentation gap and preferably previewing it, apply the chosen library extension. Installs the package and updates the OTel hook, package.json, and lockfile; repeating the same extension is a no-op.

version.description: Semver range for the instrumentation package, e.g. "^6.0.0"

registration_snippet.description: The JS/TS snippet to splice into the instrumentations array, e.g. "instrumentations.push(new PrismaInstrumentation())"

project.description: Project name when the core hosts more than one (set NEAT_PROJECTS=...). Omit to use the default project.

tools.name: neat_dry_run_extension
tools.description: Before filling an instrumentation gap, preview the extension. Returns the exact file diff, dependencies, and install command without changing the project.

version.description: Semver range for the instrumentation package, e.g. "^6.0.0"

registration_snippet.description: The JS/TS snippet to splice into the instrumentations array

project.description: Project name when the core hosts more than one (set NEAT_PROJECTS=...). Omit to use the default project.

tools.name: neat_rollback_extension
tools.description: If a library extension needs reversing, remove its package.json dependency and hook registration. Returns the rollback result; run the package manager afterward because this tool does not refresh the lockfile.

library.description: The library whose instrumentation should be rolled back

project.description: Project name when the core hosts more than one (set NEAT_PROJECTS=...). Omit to use the default project.

tools.name: neat_list_connectable
tools.description: When a hosted graph lacks provider-side evidence, list the providers this project can connect. Returns control-plane options, or a configuration note when NEAT_CP_URL and a neat_pat_ NEAT_API_KEY are unavailable.

tools.name: neat_connect
tools.description: When authorized to add hosted provider evidence, connect a listed provider with its API credential. The control plane verifies and seals the credential; the daemon then polls or receives the supported telemetry into OBSERVED. Hosted only.

credential.description: The provider's own API token — e.g. a Supabase Management token (sbp_...) or a Railway account/team token. Sealed at rest; never stored in the graph or returned.

tools.name: neat_connection_status
tools.description: When provider evidence is absent or stale in a hosted graph, inspect connections and their connecting, healthy, error, or needs-reconnect status. Returns control-plane state, not a live graph traversal.

tools.name: neat_disconnect
tools.description: When authorized to remove a hosted provider integration, disconnect it and drop its stored connection. Returns the control-plane result; this changes future provider evidence, not source code.

instructions:
NEAT does the investigation for this software system so you spend your effort on the code. It answers from a live graph fusing code, data, infrastructure, runtime traffic, incidents, and supported provider telemetry at the finest grain the evidence allows. These are NEAT's MCP tools (mcp__neat__*); load them before you reach for a shell.

Start here when a system is failing, slow, crashing, or misbehaving. First call: investigate with the service or the symptom — one call composes the incident: the recorded failure with its deploy/env context, the likely cause and its provenance, the blast radius, the governing policies, and where declared and observed behavior diverge. If you already have the exact node, get_incident_card composes the same card; if you do not yet know what is failing, ask a plain-language question first. For detail: get_incident_history and get_root_cause on the failing node, get_divergences for declared-versus-observed drift, get_graph_diff for what changed, get_blast_radius and get_dependencies before an edit, expand and relate to test the cause one hop at a time. Reach for kubectl, logs, or grep after NEAT, or for what the graph does not model.

Every claim carries provenance and confidence: EXTRACTED from source or config, OBSERVED from spans or supported provider signals, INFERRED from a bounded stitch, STALE when a once-seen edge goes quiet. A cluster read (kubectl get pods, a log tail) shows what the system looks like right now; NEAT reads what it actually did over time, fused to the exact service, file, and symbol — plus the declared-versus-observed divergence, the blast radius across observed edges, and the code locus of the failure, which a cluster read has no source for. One investigate call is the cheaper path to that answer.

Trust each result by its provenance and stop once the fault is localized — the failing node and what is wrong with it. A graph answer is not a live call to a provider, and missing observations do not prove a path never runs. Use Read/Grep for comments, arbitrary literals, config minutiae, unsupported syntax, and repositories without a graph.
